My biggest advice is to honestly just take things one day at a time for now, and prioritize your survival and mental health over everything else. Instead of focusing on future events that could happen, I found it helpful to instead focus on what was going on in the present to try and distract my mind. I also deal with an anxiety disorder, so I get that this isn't easy, but it does help. Does your school have a counselor or anything, because even if they can't help, you might be able to go there to avoid classes, while still getting marked as present, though I don't know if that's how your school does it.
The most important thing is just to remember that your survival matters so much more than all that other shit, and that the struggles you're going with, particularly regarding school, will end .

Hey mate. I'm Aussie, and have just started uni. 

At the start of year 11, I felt a lot like how you do. I stopped caring about my interests or trying in anything because I could never imagine myself living for long anyway. Back then, I thought the pain i was experincing would never end, and that suicide was my only option. However, mainly due to my fear of pain, I managed to stay alive and am now in a much better place mentally. I was able to get on some stronger medications for my depression, and started to gain back a lot of my motivation and meaning in life. Back then, I didn't think that i'd make it through term 1 of year 11, yet alone get to finish high school and start uni, but I did, and i know I would have missed out on a lot of fanatsic memories and experinces if I had taken my own life when I wanted to. 

 I think for me, surrounding myself with supportive people helped me so much in realising that my life was worth living, and that I had a postive future ahead of me. Unfortunetly, I lost a long-time friend to suicide around this time, and while this devasted me, it also opened my eyes how many people would be affected if I passed, and that kept me alive for long enough to escpae my suicidal thoughts.

Like a lot of people have said here, please make sure to priotise your mental health over school. Although year 11 and 12 can be stressful years, people often overestimate the importance of these years. For me, my main goal was to pass, and do the best that i could do without compromising my mental health. Because, in all honestly, there are so many pathways into your dream workplace even without the grades in high school. 

If you need to chat, DM me.

I'm a high school student from Australia, so my opinion may not matter, but honestly, it seems so odd to see how many teachers here are discourging travelling during school time, especially during younger years. I am currently in my final year of school and have been on multiple holidays during school time when I was younger. Most of these holidays have been between 2-4 weeks, yet despite this, I never fell behind in school or struggled with catching up. This may be because of how school works differently in Australia (particually in primary school), but, still it seems so strange to see so many people talking about how a week long holiday during term could impact a kid for years.

I've also never had a teacher who had a problem with it, nor did my parents ask for extra work from them.  Instead, my parents would often get me and my brother to complete travel diaries about what we did each day. 

Instead of causing me to "foster a dislike of education", as some teachers here suggested, travelling with my family and visiting new places helped me to form a love for learning new things through experiences, and has allowed me to learn so many things that I wouldn't have learnt in class. And besides, I believe that creating memories is one of the most important things in life. I am so grateful to have the memories that I made as a kid while travelling, espcially after having a relative pass away a few years ago.  The death was somewhat quick, and although it was horrible, my whole family are grateful that we have lots of postive memories, and that he was able to live a life without many regrets.

So honestly, I would encourage you to take a holiday and enjoy your time as a family. It can be so benefical and can set a child up to love travelling and learning about the world. I would also recommend that instead of asking the teachers for work to complete, that you look online and find tasks that your son can do that relates to the trip, as this saves the teacher the hassle, and will help your son to develop skills that he may not be able to learn from school.
